sentences: The detective is a fictional creation, the central character in a series of short stories written by the doctor and published in the magazine.
The doctor conceives of the detective as a way for him to solve crimes incognito, as he views detective work as merely a hobby and does not want the attention it would bring to his medical career.
However, when the reading public demand to actually see the detective, the doctor hires a washed-up stage actor, the performer, to play the part.
The performer slowly learns to memorise the doctor's exacting, detailed instructions every step of the way and manages to convince the public that he is indeed the detective.
After a major case, the performer oversteps his boundaries with the doctor, who fires him.
Realising that he should have been honest from the start, the doctor decides to write the detective out of his stories and replace him with a new character, "the physician sleuth", based on himself.

Unfortunately, the idea of a physician rather than a detective solving crimes is rejected by the public, and when the doctor attempts to investigate a crime of arson at a paper warehouse, he quickly finds that no one is willing to share information or co-operate with his inquiries.
Soon after, the British government contacts the doctor, requesting that the detective solve a major theft.
A government mint recently reported the disappearance of printing plates for £5 banknotes, with the printing supervisor, the printer, having gone missing on the night of the robbery.
The counterfeiting of these notes would cause the inevitable collapse of the economy if they were allowed to circulate.
The doctor is therefore forced to hunt down a drunken performer and clean him up before accepting the case.
The police force's inspector is jealous of the detective and refuses to let him or the doctor participate in the official investigation.

Rather than relying on the regular police, therefore, the doctor turns to the twelve-year-old street urchin, the boy, the leader of a street gang that he calls the "street irregulars", paying them to keep an eye on people and locate evidence.

One line of enquiry leads the doctor to the printer's daughter, the young woman, whom he and the womanising detective invite back to their quarters to recover from the shock of false evidence of her father's death.
The doctor and the detective discover that the master criminal the professor is behind the theft and find him on the docks while receiving a consignment of printing ink.
The doctor is apparently killed and the detective is left to rely on himself, using everything he has learned to solve the case.
The trail takes him to an abandoned theatre where the forgeries are being printed.
There, he discovers that the doctor is still alive after all and the two team up to defeat the professor for good and recover the missing plates.
In the process, the young woman turns out to be an imposter in the pay of the professor.
When they return to their lodgings, the detective announces to a reception committee of reporters that he intends to retire and gives full credit to the qualities of his partner the doctor.
For his part, the doctor assures the public that, far from this being the end, the team of the detective and the doctor will continue their detective work from now on as friends.
Following the closure of his old school in the countryside, a young newcomer is transferred to the city's academy, where the young detective befriends him immediately.
The young detective's mentors there include the inventor, an eccentric retired professor to whom the school has given a large attic space for his inventions, which include a flying machine.
The inventor's niece the young lady and the young detective are in love.
Elsewhere in the city, a hooded figure with a blowpipe shoots a gentleman and a clergyman with thorns that induce nightmarish hallucinations, causing their apparent suicides.
The young detective brings his suspicions of foul play to the police force detective the officer, who rebuffs him.
After rival student the classmate, who is jealous of the young detective and the young lady, frames him for cheating on an exam, the young detective is expelled from the academy.
He has one last duel with the teacher, the fencing instructor.
While the young detective says goodbye to the newcomer, the inventor is shot with a thorn and stabs himself.
Dying, he whispers the word "the avenger" to the young detective.
The young detective, the newcomer and the young lady secretly investigate the murders, uncovering the existence of the sect, an ancient Egyptian cult of deity worshippers.
The trio track the cult to a city paraffin warehouse and a secret underground wooden pyramid, where they interrupt the sacrifice of a young girl.
The sect shoot them with thorns and they escape to a cemetery to endure the hallucinations.
Back in the inventor's loft, the young detective and the newcomer find a drawing of six men, including the three victims and a fourth man, the survivor, who is still alive.

That night, the young detective and the newcomer go to see the survivor, who explains that in his youth, he and the other five men were in a foreign land, where they looted an underground pyramid containing the tombs of five Egyptian princesses.
The resulting protest was violently put down by the British Army.
A local boy named the avenger and his sister vowed to seek revenge for their parents' deaths in the protests, and replace the bodies of the five princesses with five British girls.
As they return to the school, a chance remark by the newcomer causes the young detective to realize that the avenger is none other than the teacher.
The teacher and his sister, school nurse the matron, abduct the young lady to use as the final sacrifice.
Using the inventor's flying machine, the young detective and the newcomer reach the warehouse just in time to rescue the young lady and burn the pyramid down.
When the teacher tries to shoot the young detective, the young lady shields the young detective with her body and is mortally wounded.
In a resulting duel, the teacher falls into the frozen river.
The young detective transfers to another school and the newcomer gives him an antique pipe that he bought during the investigations as a Christmas/farewell present.
An end-credits scene reveals that the teacher survived.
Checking in at a hotel in an alpine country, he signs under a new name, "the arch-criminal", foreshadowing his role as the young detective's future nemesis.

In 1894, the criminal mastermind and the detective verbally spar on the steps outside the courthouse, where the criminal mastermind has just been acquitted on a charge of murder owing to lack of evidence.
The detective remarks, "You have a magnificent brain, criminal mastermind.
I admire it so much I'd like to present it, pickled in alcohol, to the city medical society."
"It would make an impressive exhibit," replies the criminal mastermind.
The detective and the doctor are visited at their lodgings by the young woman.

She tells him that her brother the young man has received a strange note: a drawing of a man with an albatross hanging around his neck, identical to one received by her father just before his brutal murder ten years before.
The detective deduces that the note is a warning and rushes to find the young man.
He is too late, as the young man has been murdered by being strangled and having his skull crushed.
The detective, disguised as a music-hall entertainer, attends a garden party, where he correctly believes an attempt will be made on the young woman's life.

Hearing her cries from a nearby park, he captures her assailant, who turns out to be the miner's son, out for revenge on the family for the murder of his father by the young woman's father in a dispute over ownership of their South American mine.
His murder weapon was a bola.
The miner's son also reveals that it was the criminal mastermind who urged him to seek revenge.
The detective realises that the criminal mastermind is using the case as a distraction from his real crime, one that will stir the British Empire: an attempt to steal the royal jewels.
The detective rushes to the fortress, where, during a struggle, the criminal mastermind falls, presumably to his death.

In the end, the young woman is married and the detective tries to shoo a fly by playing the violin, only to have the doctor swat it with his newspaper, remarking, "Elementary, my dear detective, elementary."
The detective and the doctor learn of the death by heart attack of a nobleman.
The detective deduces the culprit to be the extortionist, the most feared blackmailer in the city, who leaked evidence of the widow's infidelity after she refused to pay.
The detective's older brother the official recruits the pair to deal with a similar case of the bride-to-be, set to be married.
The extortionist hears of the official's request through an informant at the gentlemen's club and confronts the two at their city residence.
The detective and the doctor attempt to reason with and then intimidate the extortionist, but realize they have no legal course of action if they wish to preserve the bride-to-be's marriage.
The two break into the extortionist's manor, but leave many pieces of evidence due to their inexperience.
The detective finds the bride-to-be's letters but the two are forced to hide after the extortionist returns to the study.
He meets with a new potential informant, only for her to reveal herself as the vengeful widow and shoot the extortionist, taking a strange letter to the extortionist with her.
The detective destroys several stacks of letters including the bride-to-be's and the pair flee, though the doctor loses a shoe in the process.
They confront the widow over the event and receive the letter to the extortionist in return, marked with an "M" monogram formed from four crossed sabers.

Investigating various leads with an "M" surname, the detective and the doctor come upon the marksman, an expert sharpshooter and tiger hunter, who is confronted by one young gambler over the marksman cheating at a card game.

The detective is taken to the true originator of the "M" monogram, the professor, who reveals the extortionist's operation to have been just one chapter of an international crime organization headed by the professor and centered in the city.
The professor confronts the detective with evidence of his involvement with the extortionist's death, only for the detective to daze the professor and escape with the evidence.
The detective and the doctor flee to an alpine country after their home is firebombed by the professor's men.
The detective states the evidence he provided to the inspector means the professor's ring is mere days away from being dissolved.
While visiting the waterfall, the doctor is called away by reports of a medical emergency at their hotel.
The professor confronts the detective for single combat, ready to die if it means defeating the detective.
The marksman, revealed to be another accomplice, appears as the pair fight.
The professor falls to his death after being wrestled to the edge, but the marksman fires at the detective's hands as he appears to lose his grip and fall to his own death.
The doctor realizes the emergency to have been fabricated by the detective and rushes back to the waterfall, only to find he was too late.
He finds a final letter to him from the detective, declaring the professor to have been the greatest case of his career and instructing the doctor to monitor the young gambler.
The doctor attempts to keep an eye on the young gambler, but draws suspicion in the ineptitude of his disguise.

The young gambler is murdered in locked room by a revolver round through the open window, an impossibility given the distance of the nearest building, and the doctor's obsession with the young gambler marks him as the primary suspect.

The detective reveals his survival to the doctor and the landlady, explaining that while his destruction of the professor's ring was largely successful, the marksman and a number of other members remained at large, preventing his return.

They allow the marksman's henchman to spot the detective and arrange a trap for the marksman with a lifelike wax sculpture of the detective sitting in his study, which the marksman shoots with a custom soundless air-gun before being arrested by the detective.
Discussing their adventures by the fire, the detective explains he had spotted a ledge beneath where he and the professor would fight, which he used to feign his death in order to fool the marksman.
The detective and the doctor are called to a poor district after learning about a series of strange murders only two years after the serial killer murders in the same neighborhood.
The local belief is that the killings are the work of a vampire brought back from a recent mission in a tropical country.

As they investigate the deaths, they engage in an ongoing debate about the supernatural, with the doctor believing in the possibility of vampires and the detective remaining skeptical until he is able to prove the murders are the works of a living human, rather than any undead creature.
At one point, the investigation leads them to the psychic the medium, who says that the detective will be saved by the church.
Shortly thereafter, the detective is pushed in front of a moving carriage by the supposed vampire, only to be saved by a pedestrian.

In order to catch the murderer, the detective disguises himself as a monk and reveals that the vampire was the missionary, who hoped to get revenge on the monks who didn't listen to him when he believed that the bats were causing rabies in the South American mission, when he was infected.
The film ends at the detective's home, when the landlady gives the detective his pipe, delivered by the same man that saved the detective from being run over.
When the detective asks his name, the landlady says his name was a name ending in the word church.
In 1889, the detective and the doctor.
The doctor receive a visit from the country physician, who wishes to consult them before the arrival of the young baronet, the last of the family, heir to the family estate in the county.
The country physician is anxious about letting the young baronet go to the manor, and talks about the events of the recent death of his best friend, the old baronet, the young baronet's uncle.
Although he was found dead in his garden from heart failure, the country physician noticed the footprints of a gigantic hound.

He tells the story of a supposed family curse, the legend of the hound of the family, a demonic dog that first killed a wicked ancestor several hundred years ago and is said to have caused the death of many family members in the region of the county.
Though the detective dismisses the curse, he agrees to meet the young baronet, who receives a message warning him to stay away from the moor.
The detective witnesses someone attempt to shoot the young baronet.
The detective asks the doctor to go to the manor along with the young baronet, claiming that he is too busy to accompany them himself.
The first night, the young baronet and the doctor discover the manservant, the butler, signalling from a window with a candle to someone on the moor.
After unsuccessfully catching a man fleeing across the moor, the doctor and the young baronet are startled by hound-like howls.
The next day, the doctor is suspicious of the neighbour the naturalist, a local naturalist, while the young baronet becomes attracted to the young lady, the step-sister of the naturalist.
The doctor and the young baronet attend a séance held by the country physician's wife.
In a trance, she asks, "What happened that night on the moor, old baronet?"
They are troubled by hound-like howls.
The doctor meets a crippled peddler, limping on each of his legs, and receives a message to come see him.
The peddler reveals himself to be the detective, having been on the moor all the time making his own investigation.

The hound kills a man on the moor whom the detective and the doctor fear is the young baronet but turns out to be the man the manservant was signaling to; the detective explains that it was a convicted murderer, who escaped from the nearby prison, and was the manservant's wife's brother, who had given him the young baronet's clothes.
The naturalist kept a huge, half-starved, vicious dog trained to attack individual members of the family after prolonged exposure to their scent.
When the hound is finally sent to kill the young baronet, the detective and the doctor arrive to save him just in time, killing the hound.
The naturalist traps the detective down in the hound's underground kennel, and sends the doctor on an errand to meet the detective.
The detective cuts his way out of the kennel and returns to the hall and destroys the poison that the naturalist had just given to the young baronet as a medication for his wounds.
The detective surmises that the naturalist is a member of the family, who hopes to claim their vast fortune himself after removing all other members of the bloodline.
The naturalist pulls a gun and flees.
The detective says ominously to the doctor, "He won't get very far.
I've posted constables along the roads and the only other way is across the great bog."
The detective is praised for his work on the case, and he turns in.
The detective is visited by the insurance agent, an insurance agent with a strange tale.
Seven single men, calling themselves the "club members", live together in the remote Scottish castle, near the village.
Recently one of the "club members" received a strange message, an envelope containing nothing but seven orange pips (seeds).
That night, he was murdered and his body horribly mutilated.

A few days later, a second envelope was delivered, this time containing six pips, and the recipient also died mysteriously soon afterwards, his battered corpse being recovered from the base of the cliffs.

The insurance agent holds £100,000 of life insurance policies on the seven men, and suspects that one is systematically murdering the others in order to collect the money, and begs the detective to investigate.
The detective and the doctor arrive at the scene only to find another murder has occurred, its body burned to a crisp.
The inspector also arrives to investigate.
Despite the detective's best efforts three more deaths occur, each time leaving the victim's body unrecognizable.
Meanwhile, the local tobacconist writes a message to the inspector, which already had been opened and resealed before it arrived in the inspector's possession.
The detective and the inspector went to the tobacconist's shop to investigate, only to learn the tobacconist was shot in the back before they got there.
The inspector jumps to the obvious conclusion that the last surviving member murdered all the others.

However, after the doctor goes missing, the detective has deduced the plot behind it all and leads the inspector (and the last surviving member) to a secret room where all the "club members" are hiding and the doctor is tied up.
The detective explains that the last surviving member was the victim of a plot to frame him for murder and collect the insurance money by the other six.
The tobacconist had been murdered because he had spotted one of them alive on the beach.

The master criminal (an actor) steals the famous "pearl" from the museum under the very nose of the detective and the doctor, but when the actor is caught the pearl is not found on him and he is released.
Later, the detective hears of an apparently motiveless murder.
An elderly colonel is found with his back broken amid a pile of smashed china.
The detective takes an immediate interest in the case as the unusual method of killing is that of "the killer" (another actor), known to be the master criminal's right-hand man.
Another murder occurs of an old lady, also surrounded by smashed china.
The master criminal makes two attempts to kill the detective, who surmises that the master criminal is desperately trying to recover the stolen pearl.
After a third killing, the detective finds the common feature of each: a bust of the emperor.
The master criminal, when pursued by the police, had fled through the workshop where the busts were being made and had hidden the pearl inside one of six identical busts.
The detective tracks down the vendor of the busts and finds out that one is still unaccounted for, as does the master criminal's accomplice.
The master criminal and the killer arrive at the house of the owner of the final bust, only to find that the detective has taken the owner's place.
Overpowered, the detective convinces the killer that the master criminal is responsible for the fact that the accomplice (whom the killer adores) will be hanged.
The killer turns on the master criminal and kills him, after which the detective kills the killer before the police finally arrive.
The detective smashes the final bust and recovers the pearl "with the blood of five more victims on it".
The series depicts "consulting detective" the detective (an actor) solving various mysteries in the modern-day city.

The detective is assisted in his mystery solving by his flatmate, friend and companion, the doctor (another actor), who has returned from military service in a foreign country with the army medical corps.

Although the city police force's inspector (a third actor) and others are suspicious of the detective at first, over time, his exceptional intellect and bold powers of observation persuade them of his value.
In part through the doctor's blog documenting their adventures, the detective becomes a reluctant celebrity with the press reporting on his cases and eccentric personal life.
Both ordinary people and the British government ask for his help.
Although the series depicts a variety of crimes and perpetrators, the detective's conflict with his archenemy, the master criminal (a fourth actor), is a recurring feature.
A woman (an actress), a pathologist at the hospital, occasionally assists the detective in his cases.

Other recurring roles include another actress as the housekeeper, the detective and the doctor's landlady, the series co-creator as the detective's elder brother, and the third actor as the inspector.

The doctor, seeking an apartment after returning from military service in the colonies, is recommended the vacancy at a city address by a friend of the detective, the acquaintance, who nonetheless warns of the detective's eccentric and antisocial disposition.
The doctor is amazed by the detective's forensic and deductive skills and flabbergasted by his complete ignorance on any topics not pertaining to crime and murder.
He is further unnerved by the detective's strange visitors and lack of identifiable occupation, and confides to the acquaintance that he suspects the detective of being a criminal mastermind.
The doctor challenges the detective to a boxing match, where the detective deduces the doctor's suspicions and instead identifies himself as a world-class detective.
Happy to demonstrate his profession, the detective has the doctor sit in with his next client, a fearful young woman.
The client recounts the mysterious death of her sister years earlier and fears the same fate herself after having to sleep in her sister's old room, naming her abusive stepfather as the suspect.
The doctor diagnoses the client with mere familial resentment, but is disproven when the stepfather barges in and violently threatens the two of them for interacting with the client.
The detective inspects the sister's bedroom while the stepfather is away, noting the strange ventilation shaft connecting the room with the stepfather's.

That night the detective and the doctor hide in the room with the client until the stepfather believes her to be asleep, at which point the detective lights a match and sees a venomous snake coming through the shaft.
He beats it back with a cane and breaks into the stepfather's room, where the trio find that the enraged snake had returned and fatally bitten its owner.
The detective waives the client's fee and returns home to discuss the case with the doctor by the fire.
Now with the doctor as his full-time assistant, the detective is invited by the first inspector to investigate the death of an American.
The detective finds a gold ring and deduces the case to be a murder by poisoning, but clashes with the second inspector over the direction of the investigation.

The detective advertises finding the ring and receives an elderly female visitor who claims the ring is her late husband's, only for her to steal the ring, fight her way past the doctor, and escape in a cabby.
The detective deduces the woman to have been a crossdressing accomplice and assures the doctor they are already close to the killer's identity.
The second inspector tracks down the American's correspondent and rival as the main suspect, only to find him stabbed to death in a hotel room.
The detective finds two pills at the scene and, after they are accidentally eaten by the second inspector's dog, it is found one was harmless while the other was a deadly poison.
The detective discusses the case with the doctor, the second inspector, and the first inspector only to suddenly double over in apparent pain.
A cabby is called over only for the detective to arrest the driver as the murderer.

The driver confesses in custody, explaining the American and his rival to have been religious polygamists who kidnapped the driver's fiancé for a forced marriage, leading to her death of grief and shame.
He confirms the detective's version of events, having intended for both of the victims to die by a 50/50 chance, but shows no remorse for his actions.

Discussing the case by the fire, the detective describes finding the driver's name from the American's remaining correspondence in an American city, but laments that a detective's duty is to find the truth of a crime, even if one finds the perpetrator to be more sympathetic than his victims.

The doctor reads a report on the case in the newspaper but is angered to find the credit had been given entirely to the first inspector and the second inspector, and vows to write down the detective's stories to be popularized across the world.
